entities.name: 23S rRNA gene
observations: Macrolide resistance-associated mutations in Treponema pallidum include A2058G and A2059G; these are numbered in the Escherichia coli 23S rRNA reference system.
Both mutations were linked to in-vivo azithromycin treatment failure in contemporary clinical strains.

entities.name: Syphilis
observations: Treponema pallidum clinical strains show geographically heterogeneous macrolide resistance, commonly inferred from 23S rRNA A2058G or A2059G mutations.

entities.name: Azithromycin
observations: Azithromycin failed in vivo against six Seattle Treponema pallidum clinical strains carrying A2058G or A2059G, while three wild-type strains were cured; benzathine penicillin cured mutant-strain infections.
Clinical surveillance commonly treats A2058G/A2059G detection as evidence of macrolide resistance, although many studies lack culture-based MIC testing.

entities.name: 23S mutations confer resistance
observations: In a 2016 study of six Seattle clinical strains collected in 2004–2005, all strains carrying A2058G or A2059G failed azithromycin treatment, whereas three wild-type strains were cured; the authors concluded either mutation confers in-vivo macrolide resistance.

entities.name: A2058G surveillance prevalence
observations: A2058G was detected at high prevalence in contemporary clinical surveillance: 75/141 US samples (53%), 194/211 Chinese patients (91.9%), 83/93 Amsterdam samples (88%), 97.5% in Hunan, and 38/38 detectable samples in Xiamen.

entities.name: Geographic resistance heterogeneity
observations: Resistance-associated mutation prevalence is not universal: Madagascar found no evidence of azithromycin resistance, Canada reported 4/14 resistant PCR-positive cases, and Buenos Aires reported 45.7% resistance in 2015–2019.
